headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the financial burden of grid infrastructure and capacity costs from residential ratepayers to large energy users, such as data centers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, some state legislators.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Dominion-Backed Bills. All Eyes on Regulators Now.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and allowing Dominion Energy to spend on burying distribution lines. This aims to address rising capacity costs on the grid, which have contributed to increased customer bills.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, enhancing transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden, though some acknowledge the need for transparency).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making this information publicly accessible. This transparency measure aims to provide credible data for water supply planning, especially during droughts, and address concerns about the industry's growing water demands.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to potential restrictions and increased assessment costs).
news_headline: As data center noise concerns grow, Loudoun Co. officials discuss possible mitigation efforts
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are increasingly concerned about persistent noise from data centers, with complaints about a 'tonal' hum causing headaches and sleep disruption. Local officials are exploring legislative avenues, including changes to zoning and noise ordinances, to mitigate these impacts, as current ordinances may not adequately address tonal noise.
